who: Walter Struve, historian of Germany and German migration, City University of New York.

evidence.says: The publisher identifies Walter Struve, author of Germans and Texans, as Professor of History at the City University of New York.
A 1979 review credits Walter Struve at City College, City University of New York, writing on German history.
The authority identifies Walter Struve through Die Republik Texas, Bremen und das Hildesheimische (1983), consistent with the CUNY historian and his German-Texan research.

notes: Institution and historical field agree. The other records concern a chemistry author (n88069149) and the author of a State Library of Victoria staffing report (nb91061052).

who: John E. Sunder (John Edward Sunder), historian of the American West, University of Texas at Austin.

evidence.says: The university identifies John Sunder as professor emeritus of history, who joined UT Austin in 1956 to teach Western history and published books on the Missouri River fur trade.
The publisher lists John E. Sunder as author of Joshua Pilcher, Fur Trader and Indian Agent and The Fur Trade on the Upper Missouri, 1840-1865.
The authority expands John E. Sunder to John Edward Sunder and cites Joshua Pilcher, fur trader and Indian agent (1968).

notes: University, field, and the authority-linked publication identify the same historian.

who: Paul Robinson Sweet, historian of Germany, Michigan State University; PhD Wisconsin 1934.

evidence.says: Princeton University Library's finding aid identifies Paul Robinson Sweet and states that he received his history PhD from Wisconsin in 1934; his thesis became Friedrich Von Gentz, Defender of the Old Order.
The April 19, 1968 university newspaper reports the appointment of Paul R. Sweet as professor of history, effective September 1.
The authority expands Paul R. Sweet to Paul Robinson Sweet and identifies him through Wilhelm von Humboldt (1978-1980).

notes: The Wisconsin doctorate matches exactly, and the Michigan State appointment supports the advising affiliation.

who: Peter A. Szok, historian of modern Central America, Texas Christian University; PhD Tulane 1998.

evidence.says: TCU lists Peter Szok as professor of history, with a Tulane PhD in 1998, and includes La última gaviota among his books.
The Folk Art Society of America identifies Peter Szok as associate professor of history at TCU in a 2013 author entry.
The authority identifies Peter A. Szok as the author of La última gaviota (2001).

notes: Exact doctorate institution and year; matching employer, field, and book establish the authority match.

who: Molly Taylor-Poleskey, early modern European and digital historian, Middle Tennessee State University 2016-2023; PhD Stanford 2016.

evidence.says: Her CV lists a Stanford history PhD in 2016, assistant professor at MTSU from August 2016 to spring 2022, and associate professor from August 2022 to July 2023. It lists The Great Elector’s Table (2024).
The authority identifies Molly Taylor-Poleskey through The Great Elector’s table (2024).

notes: Exact doctorate match and MTSU employment covering 2022; the book links the candidate authority to the same CV.

who: Apparently Bettye Collier-Thomas, Temple University historian of women and African American history, with a George Washington history PhD.

evidence.says: Temple lists Bettye Collier-Thomas as professor emeritus in History, with a PhD from George Washington University.

The society biography identifies Bettye Collier-Thomas as a Temple history professor, dates her George Washington history PhD to 1974, and describes her research in nineteenth- and twentieth-century women’s history.
Betty Jean Thomas is identified through Harmonic materials and treatment of dissonance in the pianoforte music of Frederic Chopin (1963).
Betty J. Thomas is identified as a nursing professional through Innovations in nursing education administration (1990).
Betty Wood Thomas has the variant Elizabeth Wood Thomas and is identified through census and genealogical publications.

notes: None of the supplied authorities identifies the Temple historian: they describe other full names and works. Supervisor identification is inferred from institution and doctorate; the society biography gives 1974 rather than the AHA record’s 1975. No supplied candidate should be linked.

who: James A. Tinsley, historian of Texas, University of Houston; PhD Wisconsin-Madison.

evidence.says: UH Libraries identifies James A. Tinsley as a UH history professor for 42 years and lists Texas Society of Certified Public Accountants, a history and his edition of Selected Letters of Harris Kempner.
The university catalogue lists James A. Tinsley as professor emeritus of history with a PhD from the University of Wisconsin at Madison.
The authority identifies James A. Tinsley through Texas Society of Certified Public Accountants (1983) and Kempner’s Selected letters (1957).

notes: Employer and doctorate institution match; two identical publications connect the authority directly to the UH historian.

who: Charles Leon Tipton, also published as C. Leon Tipton, medieval historian at Lehigh University.

evidence.says: The university chronology names Charles Tipton as history chairman in 1980-1981 and Charles L. Tipton among faculty completing 25 years of service in 1989.
A February 1983 review of 1204: The Unholy Crusade credits C. Leon Tipton at Lehigh University.
The authority for Charles Leon Tipton gives C. Leon Tipton as a variant and cites Nationalism in the middle ages (1972).

notes: The authority’s C. Leon variant is documented at Lehigh in the student’s dissertation year. Medieval history also agrees; the supplied Charles M., Charles W., and Charles D. namesakes are not this candidate.
